title: Why she cannot play note for note
summary: She always improvises, even reading Rachmaninoff.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: they've written and you have to play it then. So why should I want to play something somebody else has written? When I was a kid and my principal got all these teachers and all these things for me, I couldn't play Rachmaninoff and any of those things. I had to improvise in it. I couldn't play it the way the music was. I can't play music - when I'm reading, I have to improvise then. I hear it and see it, you know. I'm improvising then; I can't play it the way it's written. I never could play anything note for note so it wouldn't be good for me.
This I think would be your problem, because classical music is based on the fact that you play it as written; you interpret it but you play it as written.
Whereas you don't play that way.
No, I don't play that way at all. But a lot of musicians can. Dizzy can; he can play note for note and things, but I can't. I have to improvise or add something.
